=== butokuden.png ===
Original Taiwanese game art for "Tainan Gazetteer" (府城夜巡地圖), set in Tainan around 1930.
Style: handmade layered paper sculpture (紙雕 / kirie), the same for buildings, trees, plants,
fences and props. Every shape is a piece of cut paper: visible paper fibres, slightly soft
hand-cut edges, pieces overlapping in shallow layers with small soft contact shadows where one
sheet sits on another. Colour is printed on the paper: clearly visible risograph / stencil print
grain and uneven ink density across every flat area, never a clean digital fill.
Details are built from small cut pieces (roof tiles, bricks, window frames, leaves, petals,
wood planks), not painted lines.
Colour: follow the real object, then mute it: pale, slightly greyed, warm. Typical tones: warm
cream, pale brick red, coral, sage and grey-green, mustard, indigo, wood brown, stone grey.
No saturated red-against-green contrast.
Do NOT make: a 3D render or clay/plastic model, smooth bevelled relief, realistic or painterly
illustration, photo textures, thick foam layers, glow, glossy highlights, black outline strokes,
smooth gradients, depth of field.
Output: generated natively on a fully TRANSPARENT background (real alpha, no chroma-key colour
behind it, no coloured fringe), every object complete and separated by clear transparent
gutters, no ground, no base, no cast shadow outside the object, no text, no captions, no logos.
View: front-facing, very slight three-quarter, the same for every object on the sheet.

Generate one original cut-paper building sprite, centered with clear transparent margins, for request 17. Input images 1 and 2 (machiya and literature museum) are approved style references; input 3 (Shennong street house) is also a style reference. Use only their cut-paper construction, paper texture and ink treatment. Remaining inputs are photos for architectural form and muted colour only. Override the general view instruction above: strictly straight-on orthographic front elevation, perfectly level, no foreshortening, no receding sides or visible undersides, like the literature museum. Use three or four thin flat paper layers, clearly visible paper fibres and print grain in all colour fields. Compact complete silhouette, target width 1.22 times height, hard maximum width 1.4 times height. Native transparent alpha. No landscape, props, people, text, logos, or plaque lettering.

Tainan Wude Hall (臺南武德殿), central front entrance and just two window bays per side. Use the first photo for the front elevation. Broad charcoal slate-grey irimoya tiled roof with subtly upturned ends, centred triangular light trim gable with dark timber slatted vents, and a smaller shallow wave-shaped muted grey-green copper entrance canopy below it. Pale muted earth-ochre plaster walls and columns, brown lattice windows and small transoms, light stone horizontal gallery railings on the elevated main floor, visibly tall grey-brown coursed masonry foundation with small grilles and integral central front stairs. Compress the façade by omitting repeated outer bays while keeping wide flared eaves.

Look squarely at the central rounded corner entrance axis, with two short low flanking wings and one tall arched upper window in each.
